title: Research Bite #44: Practice Does Not Make Perfect – Experimental Evidence on the Effectiveness of Coaching Beginning Teachers
author: Craig Barton
summary: Research Bite #44 summarizes Cohen, Wong, Liu, Wilson, Yonas, and Parten's multisite randomized controlled trial testing whether directive coaching or self-reflection better improves beginning teachers' skills after mixed-reality simulation practice. Across 292 novice teachers at three demographically distinct US teacher-preparation programs, the researchers compared coaching against the more common practice of self-reflection on two teaching tasks: providing text-based instructional feedback and redirecting off-task student behavior. Coaching consistently and robustly improved behavioral-redirection skills across all three sites, and coached novices were also less quick to judge minor misbehavior harshly. Coaching's effect on the more complex, content-focused feedback task was far less consistent, particularly for novices in an alternative-licensure program, suggesting some instructional skills may need more than short coaching sessions to shift. The clear message for teacher preparation is that practice alone is not enough — simulated rehearsal paired with expert, directive feedback beats self-reflection, especially for classroom management, but coaching is not a universal fix for every category of teaching skill.
points: Directive coaching from an expert consistently outperformed self-reflection at improving novice teachers' skills, especially for redirecting off-task behavior — a large-scale multisite RCT rather than a small lab study.

Coaching's benefit was far less consistent for complex, content-focused feedback tasks, particularly among novices in an alternative-licensure program, suggesting some skills need more than brief coaching to shift.
Novices often struggle to self-reflect effectively without external guidance, potentially lacking the schema to identify areas for improvement or overestimating their own abilities.

The core implication for teacher preparation: practice through simulation alone is not sufficient — it needs to be paired with expert, directive feedback, since self-reflection alone does not reliably produce the same gains.
